findings.claim: The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment estimated these services are worth over $33 trillion a year - roughly the size of the entire global economy.
findings.truth: The $33 trillion figure is from Costanza et al., 'The value of the world's ecosystem services and natural capital', Nature 387 (1997): a range of $16-54 trillion a year, average $33 trillion. It is not a Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (2005) figure. The paper compared it with global GNP of about $18 trillion a year, so it was nearly double the world economy, not the same size.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Ecosystem services' (1997 peer-reviewed study, average US$33 trillion/yr, Costanza and colleagues, not the MEA); Costanza et al. Nature 387:253-260 (1997)

findings.claim: Fabricated examiner claims in seven lessons: 'Naming circulation cells lifts a 2-mark answer to 4. Examiners reward precise terms...' (L1); 'examiners want named drivers' (L2); 'examiners want at least two distinct causes' (L3); 'examiners want named strategies' (L5); 'Examiners reward students who pair specific events with specific price moves' (L6); 'examiners reward answers that combine three things' (L7); 'Examiners reward students who weave wider knowledge into the answer' (L8 content) and the same phrase as a flashcard answer (L8).
findings.truth: None of these describes anything the specification or a published mark scheme states. Rewritten as direct advice to the student, keeping the same substance and no invented mark uplift.
findings.evidence: checker brief: invented examiner claims are FIX; spec assessment sections carry no such statements

findings.claim: Lessons 1-7 each label their extended-writing question '(8 marks plus 4 SPaG)', and lessons 2-6 add a 'SPaG (4)' band line to the mark scheme.
findings.truth: Paper 3 carries 64 raw marks of which up to 4 in total, for the whole paper, are for spelling, punctuation, grammar and specialist terminology. Seven separate questions cannot each carry 4 SPaG marks. The SPaG marks sit with the Section D decision question, which lesson 8 already labels as 12 marks. Labels reduced to '(8 marks)' and the SPaG band lines removed.
findings.evidence: spec, Component 3 assessment overview (lines 345-380) and Topic 9 assessment information: 'up to 4 marks are awarded for spelling, punctuation, grammar and their use of specialist terminology'

findings.claim: China overtook the United States as the world's largest energy consumer in 2009 and India is on track to do the same by 2030.
findings.truth: India is the world's third-largest energy consumer and the IEA does not project it overtaking the United States by 2030. What the IEA does say is that India sees the largest increase in energy demand of any country to 2040.
findings.evidence: IEA India Energy Outlook 2021: 'India is the world's third-largest energy consuming country'; largest increase in demand of any country to 2040

findings.claim: Tropical rainforests cover only about 6% of the Earth's surface.
findings.truth: About 6% is the share of the Earth's LAND surface. Tropical rainforest is under 3% of the Earth's total surface, because oceans cover about 71% of the planet.
findings.evidence: standard forest-area figures (about 13-14 million km2 of rainforest against 149 million km2 of land and 510 million km2 total surface); recomputation

findings.claim: Warmer winters allow pests like the spruce bark beetle to survive and multiply: in British Columbia, beetles have killed about half of the merchantable lodgepole pine since the 1990s.
findings.truth: The British Columbia epidemic that killed about half the province's merchantable lodgepole pine from the 1990s was the mountain pine beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae). The spruce beetle (Dendroctonus rufipennis) is a different species that attacks spruce. A student naming the wrong species in a named-example answer loses the credit.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia 'Mountain pine beetle': Dendroctonus ponderosae, British Columbia epidemic from the 1990s, about half the province's lodgepole pines killed by 2008; spruce beetle confirmed as a distinct species

findings.claim: By 2014, soy expansion accounted for less than 1% of new Amazon deforestation, down from over 30%.
findings.truth: The 30% to 1% fall is the share of NEW SOYA AREA planted on recently cleared forest, before and after the 2006 Soy Moratorium. It is not the share of Amazon deforestation caused by soya; Amazon clearance is dominated by cattle ranching, and soya has never been about 30% of it.
findings.evidence: Gibbs et al., 'Brazil's Soy Moratorium', Science 347 (2015): soy expansion into forest fell from about 30% of new soy area to about 1%

findings.claim: 'The Edexcel B the people-and-environment unit paper ends with a 12-mark decision-making essay' and the flashcard 'How many marks is the the people-and-environment unit decision essay?'
findings.truth: Both sentences carry a duplicated article left by an automated rename and do not read. Repaired without changing meaning.

findings.claim: Lessons 1 and 2 (Topic 7, Section A) and lessons 3, 4 and 5 (Topic 8, Section B) each set an 8-mark extended-writing question.
findings.truth: The specification names 8-mark extended writing only for Section C (Topic 9, consuming energy resources) and a 12-mark extended-writing decision for Section D. It does not say Sections A and B carry 8-mark questions, but nor does it rule out extended writing there, and Section B in practice carries longer open response. Options: (a) leave the 8-markers as useful extended-writing practice on the right content, or (b) rescale the Topic 7 and Topic 8 items to shorter open-response forms. Not edited.
findings.evidence: spec, Component 3 assessment overview: 'Section C will include 8-mark extended writing questions and Section D will offer a choice of one from three decisions assessed through a 12-mark extended writing question'

findings.claim: Every lesson sets a '4 marks - Calculate' question, with a four-step band ladder for one-step arithmetic (for example 2,400 divided by 12).
findings.truth: Every calculation in the unit is arithmetically correct (recomputed: 200 mm; 300%; 80%; 15%; 26 percentage points; 267.5%; $750; 720 km2). Only the mark weight looks inflated for a paper whose calculations are typically 1-2 marks. Not worth an edit on its own.
findings.evidence: recomputation of all eight calculation items

findings.claim: The Sudbury smelter in Ontario killed thousands of square kilometres of forest.
findings.truth: Published Sudbury figures are in the hundreds of square kilometres of barren and semi-barren land (about 3,350 ha rehabilitated and about 30,000 ha still to rehabilitate by 2010, so roughly 330 km2), though wider vegetation damage is reported over a larger area. The true total is not settled enough to correct.

findings.claim: The taiga and its frozen soils together store more carbon than any other land biome on Earth - perhaps twice as much as the rainforests.
findings.truth: The settled version of this claim is per unit area: boreal forest stores more carbon per hectare than tropical forest, largely in soils and permafrost. Total-store comparisons vary between studies, so 'twice as much' is not settled. The sentence is already hedged with 'perhaps'.
findings.evidence: boreal vs tropical carbon-stock literature is not settled on the total ratio

findings.claim: Indonesia has slowed but not reversed loss after a 2019 moratorium on new palm-oil licences.
findings.truth: The palm-oil permit moratorium was Presidential Instruction 8/2018, signed September 2018. A separate moratorium on new permits in primary forest and peatland, which also bites on palm oil, was made permanent in August 2019. Both readings are defensible, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Indonesian Presidential Instruction 8/2018 (Sept 2018) and the August 2019 permanent forest moratorium

findings.claim: Mark-scheme bullet: 'REDD payments helped Brazil reduce Amazon deforestation by 80% between 2004 and 2012, with Norwegian funding.'
findings.truth: The 80% fall is real (27,772 km2 in 2004 to 4,571 km2 in 2012) but is mainly credited to Brazilian enforcement, satellite monitoring and the soy and beef moratoria; the Amazon Fund only began in 2008. The bullet overstates REDD's role but sits in a list of arguments a student may offer.
findings.evidence: INPE PRODES deforestation series; Amazon Fund established 2008

findings.claim: The Food and Agriculture Organization estimates global food demand will be 60% higher in 2050 than it was in 2010.
findings.truth: The FAO 60% projection uses a 2005/2007 baseline, not 2010. The later FAO figure against a 2012 baseline is about 50%. The direction and order of magnitude are right, so no edit.

findings.claim: Mark-scheme bullet: 'UK gas was 50% from Norway in 2022'.
findings.truth: Norway supplied roughly 60% of UK gas IMPORTS in 2022, not 50% of total UK gas supply, a large share of which is still produced domestically. Imprecise rather than wrong enough to correct without a settled figure.

findings.claim: Two small internal inconsistencies: the climate-graph panel gives equatorial rainforest '200+ mm every month' where the main text gives '2,000+ mm' a year (about 167 mm a month); and the key fact says rising Ferrel-cell air at 60 degrees gives temperate forest, where the biome at 60 degrees is boreal forest.
findings.truth: Both are textbook simplifications rather than errors that would cost marks. Left alone.
findings.evidence: internal comparison; standard biome latitude bands

summary: One HIGH finding: lesson 4 names the spruce bark beetle for the British Columbia lodgepole pine epidemic, which was the mountain pine beetle, and the wrong species is repeated in a knowledge check, a flashcard and a mark scheme. The rest are exam-form and attribution problems: seven lessons label an 8-mark question '(8 marks plus 4 SPaG)' when the whole paper carries only 4 SPaG marks, eight fabricated examiner claims across seven lessons, the $33 trillion ecosystem-services figure credited to the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment instead of Costanza et al. 1997, an incorrect claim that India will overtake the United States as the largest energy consumer by 2030, rainforest area given as 6% of the Earth's surface rather than its land surface, and the Soy Moratorium's 30% to 1% fall attached to the wrong denominator. All 40 knowledge-check keys, all 5 matching sets and all 8 calculations were recomputed and are correct.
